plate.narration: The rush road has stopped at the ford. Wagon wheels sink into ruts while a centaur hurries past with line tokens. Somewhere ahead, the river is deciding who gets across. First, everyone has to wait their turn.

objectives.label: Put the centaur markers back up
Helped the Bracken family get home
Shared supper with the cinder wolves

goal.text: Wait your turn at the river ford, then try to get across.

steps.label: Help someone stuck in the line
Spend the night in the line
Take your turn at the ford

facet_ford.name: The Ford Stone
facet_ford.text: Wrapped in a witch's wool sock. It rings every bell charm it passes, and won't stop.

charm_ford_witch.name: Mother Thrum's Tuned Charm
charm_ford_witch.text: A bell charm tuned to the note the stones hum. Hold it near a gem and it sings.

scene_parade.narration: Marda's rumor board said the rush road was jammed but moving. Tonight, wait your turn at the river ford, then try to get across. Wagons fill the ruts. Centaur relay-runners weave between them. The parade stops. Ahead, somebody shouts, "NUMBERS! GET YOUR NUMBERS!"

choices.label: Walk up to the front and see why
Read the crowd like a book
Sniff the gem wagons

scene_parade_sniff_wagons.narration: Your dragonling sniffs the nearest gem wagon and goes very still. It smells of home: warm rock, ash, the inside of a cave. And underneath that, a hum you can feel in your teeth. Every wagon in the parade smells the same, all the way to the front.

choices.label: Walk on up the column

scene_parade_read_crowd.narration: Your kitsune reads the line the way other people read a menu. That wagon is two places ahead of where it should be. That man is selling the same pebble twice. Those three are a family and that one only says she is. By the time you are halfway up the column, you know the whole line's business, and the line does not know you know.

choices.label: Walk on up the column

scene_spilled_pannier.narration: A wagon wheel drops into a rut. Its pannier splits, spilling gem chips. The lead drover, who runs the river crossing, booms "WATCH YOUR BOOTS!" Catch and pass the pannier to earn his help, or stand back and watch what the chips do.

choices.label: Make a catch-and-pass line for the spilled chips
Hold back and watch the scramble
Spot every last chip, even the ones in the mud
Risk a quick scoop before the crowd moves

check_catch_chips.prompt: Everybody scoop up the rolling gem chips before the crowd does

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and pass, scoop and pass, and every chip is back in the pannier before a single pocket gets one. The drover counts them twice, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

onFailure.narration: You scoop up a whole double handful, very proudly, and give the drover three chips and a great deal of gravel. He laughs so hard his hat falls off. By the time he finds it, the crowd has pocketed the rest.

scene_spilled_pannier_hold_back.narration: You stand back. The crowd scrambles, squabbles and stuffs its pockets. Nobody notices what you notice: every chip in the dust is trembling, very faintly, like a kettle a long way off. When the last chip is gone, the road goes quiet.

choices.label: Walk on to the front

scene_spilled_pannier_spot_all.narration: Your bigfoot stops, looks once, and points. Under the wheel. In a hoofprint. Inside somebody's boot. Every chip goes back in the pannier, even the one the dog was guarding. The drover stares. "Never seen eyes like that," he booms. "I'll remember you folks."

choices.label: Walk on to the front

scene_number_pebble.narration: At the west branch, the ford line is two days long. A faun provisioner named Burdock sells numbered pebbles and very expensive honeycakes. Your pebble says 412. "My lucky number!" says Burdock. The ford is on number 9.

choices.label: Buy a very expensive honeycake
Pocket your pebble and look around

scene_number_pebble_buy_cake.narration: Three coins buy a honeycake the size of one coin. "My lucky number," says Burdock, meaning your money. You save the cake for someone who needs it.

choices.label: Look around the camp

scene_number_pebble_pocket_pebble.narration: You keep your coins and pebble 412. "Plenty of time to get hungry," says Burdock. His goat, Pudding, stares into the pebble bucket. Nothing good begins with a goat staring into a bucket.

choices.label: Look around the camp

choice_runaway_goat.narration: Burdock's goat, Pudding, gallops down the line with the pebble bucket on her head. Numbers fly everywhere. "My bucket! My GOAT!" wails Burdock. Chase her, sort the spilled numbers for a honeycake, or use a crumb to tempt her back.

choices.label: Chase Pudding down the line
Help sort the numbers back into the bucket
Tempt Pudding with a crumb of honeycake

check_goat_chase.narration: Pudding gallops down the line with the bucket on her head. Then she skids to a stop at a cabbage stall and starts to chew, because a goat cannot walk past a cabbage. She does it every few steps. "Wait for the chew!" wails Burdock. "Then grab!"

interaction.cue: Tap when Pudding stops to chew.

onSuccess.narration: You zig when Pudding zigs and zag when she zags, and grab the bucket by its handle just as she leaps a cooking pot. Pudding thinks this was a wonderful game. For the rest of the day, wherever you go, a goat goes too. Burdock pays you three coins for the rescued bucket, and kisses Pudding on the nose.

onFailure.narration: Pudding leaps a cooking pot, a sleeping drover and a small tent. You leap the cooking pot, mostly. In the end she trots back to Burdock all by herself, very pleased, with the bucket still on her head.

choice_runaway_goat_sort.narration: You ask people for their numbers and sort the pebbles fairly. Burdock rewards you with a honeycake. "This has never happened," he says. "Tell nobody." Pudding returns while he counts.

choices.label: Dust off your knees

choice_runaway_goat_crumb.narration: Pudding eats the crumb and drops the bucket. Then she follows you. Burdock approves of this arrangement for approximately one day.

choices.label: Walk on, with a goat

scene_three_cards.narration: A kitsune named Tamsin Three-Cards shuffles on a barrel. "Find the Sun Card! Win a front-of-the-line pebble!" Her third tail twitches. You can watch the trick, walk away, or help her con the crowd for an unfair Number 1.

choices.label: Watch her tails and catch the trick
Wink at her, one fox to another
Offer to help her draw a crowd
Keep your coins and walk on by

check_expose.narration: Tamsin's hands blur and the three cards fly, left, middle, right. The Sun Card starts under the left card. Her third tail twitches every time it moves. Watch where it goes.

interaction.cue: Watch the Sun Card, then pick its card.

onSuccess.narration: Every time she shuffles, the third tail flicks the Sun Card up her sleeve. You say so, loudly and politely.

onFailure.narration: You pick the middle card with total confidence. It is a picture of a very smug fox. The crowd laughs, and so, to be fair, does she.

scene_exposed.narration: Tamsin shakes the Sun Card from her sleeve. The crowd gets its pebbles back. The drovers notice who caught the trick. They will wave you beside the lead wagon at the ford.

choices.label: Head for the smell of soup

scene_join_con.narration: You stand in the crowd and gasp very loudly every time somebody almost wins. Tamsin pays you with a front-of-the-line pebble and a wink. It is shiny and it says number 1, and it is absolutely not fair.

choices.label: Head for the smell of soup

scene_three_cards_walk_by.narration: You keep your coins. Tamsin tips her hat. "Come back when you feel lucky." Behind you, somebody loses again, very loudly.

choices.label: Head for the smell of soup

scene_soup_line.narration: A cheerful ladler named Wend gives away soup under the dark-robed helpers' tent. "Kindness first," Wend says. A little crystal on the ladle cord shivers whenever a gem wagon passes.

choices.label: Say thank you and eat up
Ask why the crystal shivers

scene_soup_line_ask_crystal.narration: "Since the red night," says Wend, lifting the crystal. "Means something, doesn't it?" Another wagon passes. The crystal hums. Wend changes the subject to soup.

choices.label: Finish your soup

scene_soup_line_thank_wend.narration: Wend beams at your thanks and fills your bowls again. No questions asked. "Kindness first." The crystal shivers at another wagon.

choices.label: Finish your soup

scene_queue_jumpers.narration: Red scarves push up the line. "Ford closes tomorrow!" their leader shouts. An old faun doubts this. Block them, fetch the drovers, or use someone who knows their tricks. If you hold the line, the scarves will owe you fair treatment.

choices.label: Stand shoulder to shoulder and hold the line
Run and fetch the drovers
Tell them, sweetly, that the back is the new front
Ask Tamsin to keep them busy

check_block_jumpers.narration: The red scarves charge up the line, elbows first. The old faun grabs your sleeve. "Link arms!" he says. Somebody takes the front of the line, and everybody braces behind.

interaction.cue: Friends brace the line while someone holds the front.

onSuccess.narration: You link arms with the old faun and two very surprised strangers, and the red scarves bounce off you like a ball off a wall. They grumble all the way back to the end of the line. The whole line cheers, and the red scarves will remember you. The old faun fishes his hat out of the soup and, dripping, gives you two coins for the trouble.

onFailure.narration: The red scarves squeeze past, all elbows. Then the last one trips over Pudding's bucket, and the whole gang goes down in a red-scarfed heap. The line laughs so hard that they slink off to the back anyway.

scene_queue_jumpers_call_drovers.narration: You run down to the ford and fetch the lead drover. He walks back up the line without hurrying, stands in front of the red scarves, and says one word. "BACK." His voice rattles the wagon wheels. They go back. The drover gives you a slow nod, and fishes the old faun's hat out of the soup.

choices.label: Back to your place in line

scene_queue_jumpers_send_back.narration: Your kitsune smiles the sweetest smile in the line. "Oh, haven't you heard? The ford moved. The back is the front now." The red scarves look at each other and then sprint, very fast, all the way to the back. It takes them an hour to work it out. By then they are too embarrassed to come back.

choices.label: Back to your place in line

scene_queue_jumpers_tamsin_help.narration: Tamsin strolls up shuffling her cards. "Find the Sun Card, win a place at the front!" The red scarves crowd around to play. They play for an hour. They never find the Sun Card. By the time they give up, the line has rolled on without them, and Tamsin gives you a wink.

choices.label: Back to your place in line

scene_relay_message.narration: A centaur relay-runner skids beside you. "Message for the drovers. Hill road next. Can't stop!" The note says RIVER RISING. CROSS SLOW. Run it, sing it down the line, or fly it to the ford.

choices.label: Run the note down to the ford
Have a duskrunner sprint the note down the line
Sing it down the line, the relay way
Fly the note straight to the ford

check_run_message.prompt: Run a message down a two-day line, with the fastest of you in front

onSuccess.narration: You weave through wagons, goats and campfires, and slap the note into the lead drover's hand. He reads it, nods, and slows the crossing to a careful walk. When you get back, the runner tosses you a brave whistle. "The relay remembers," she says.

onFailure.narration: You run as fast as you can and hand the note to the wrong drover, who reads it out loud to absolutely everybody. That, it turns out, works just as well. By lunchtime the whole line knows the river is rising.

scene_relay_message_sing.narration: You sing RIVER RISING, CROSS SLOW. The next fire sings it to the next. Soon the drovers sing back. The runner grins and gallops away.

choices.label: Listen to it roll away

scene_relay_message_fly.narration: Your griffin takes the note in a beak and is over the whole line in four wingbeats. The lead drover reads it, looks up at the river, and nods. When you land back beside the runner, she whistles. "The relay could use a friend with wings," she says, and gallops off before you can answer.

choices.label: Land back in the line

choice_tolls.narration: Choose one job in the line before dusk. Free the wagon to earn its crew's help if a load tips in the ford. Restore the marker line for an easier ford approach. Or help the Brackens, a faun family beside a cracked wheel, and earn a ride on their cart. "We are being very brave," says Littlest Bracken. You cannot do every job tonight.

choices.label: Level the wagon load and roll it out
Have a thornguard take the weight while everyone heaves
Brace and raise the fallen marker posts
Fly the marker line and spot every post
Sit down with the Brackens
Risk putting the posts back by their worn numbers

check_unmire.prompt: Everybody heave a gem wagon out of the mud

onSuccess.narration: One, two, THREE, and the wagon comes out with a noise like a giant boot leaving a puddle. The drover gives you a brave whistle and calls you "mudlarks", which is a compliment.

onFailure.narration: The wagon comes out in the end, but only after everyone has sat down in the mud at least once. You will be finding mud in your ears until next week.

check_markers.prompt: Put the markers back in the right order

onSuccess.narration: Post by post, you walk the line back into order, reading the worn numbers with your thumbs where the paint has gone. The last marker goes in with a thump, and the whole line points, straight and plain, at the one safe way down to the ford.

onFailure.narration: You put them all back up, beautifully, in the wrong order. A centaur runner gallops past, stops, laughs, and fixes them in about four seconds.

scene_markers_restored.narration: The marker line stands straight again, every post pointing the safe way to the ford. A centaur relay-runner slows down just long enough to say "The relay remembers," and then she is gone, already singing it to the next runner up the road.

choices.label: Back to camp before dusk

scene_family.narration: The Brackens' cart wheel is cracked, their season is over, and they need to get home before the river rises. The littlest Bracken is holding a line pebble with a big number on it and trying very hard not to cry about it.

choices.label: Swap pebbles, so they cross before you
Share your honeycake
Lash the wheel together with rope

scene_family_fix_wheel.narration: You lash the cracked wheel together with rope, around and around, until it looks like a wheel wearing a sweater. It turns. It wobbles, but it turns. The littlest Bracken rides on top of the cart to test it and declares it the best wheel ever made, which is not true, but it will get them home.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_family_share_cake.narration: You break the honeycake into pieces, then more pieces, so the littlest Bracken gets a bit from everyone. For a while nobody says anything, because honeycake. Then the mother says their season was not all bad, really, and the littlest one falls asleep against a cart wheel with crumbs on both cheeks.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_family_give_pebble.narration: You hand the littlest Bracken your pebble, and take theirs. Their number is enormous. Yours was not. The littlest Bracken looks at the small number for a long time and then stops trying not to cry and just cries, happily, all over it. The Brackens will cross at dawn, and they do not stop thanking you until dusk.

choices.label: Back to camp before dark

scene_dusk_wolves.narration: Cinder wolves sit beyond the firelight, cold and thin. They keep away from the humming gem wagons. Share real supper, let them be, or try driving them off. Their ears turn toward every clink of a bowl.

choices.label: Share your supper with them
Leave them be and keep your fire small
Shoo them away from the camp

scene_wolves_fed.narration: You put your supper down on a flat stone and step back. The wolves eat politely, and then the whole pack lies down in a heap by your fire, glowing like a pile of coals. It is the warmest night anybody in the line has had all week. The road will remember this.

choices.label: Follow the laughter to the big campfire

scene_dusk_wolves_leave_be.narration: You keep the fire small. The wolves stay beyond its light. At midnight one howls a long, low note. Gem wagons creak in their sleep.

choices.label: Follow the laughter to the big campfire

encounter_wolves.narration: The wolves do not want to leave. They are cold, and your fire is right there.

onVictory.narration: The pack slinks off down the line to the next fire, where somebody feeds them. The whole campsite hears about who shooed and who shared.

onDefeat.narration: The wolves win the argument, eat everybody's supper, and curl up on your bedrolls. There will be no sleeping there tonight, so you wander off, cold and hungry, toward the laughter at the big campfire.

scene_campfire_play.narration: A camp troupe acts out the red night with blankets and saucepans. Their mountain gets the hiccups. "New mountain, darlings!" cries the leader. Play it yourselves, offer what you really heard, or nominate Pudding if she followed you.

choices.label: Volunteer to play the mountain
Tell them what you really heard: the humming
Let Pudding play the mountain
Take over the play and give it a better ending

check_play_mountain.narration: The troupe leader hands you a red blanket and points at a barrel. "Climb up, darling, and be a MOUNTAIN!" The children in the front row hold their breath.

interaction.cue: Rumble, wobble and erupt until the mountain is finished.

options.label: Wobble the red blanket
options.reaction: The whole front row wobbles with you.

onSuccess.narration: You stand on a barrel under a red blanket and RUMBLE. You erupt with a sack of pinecones. Three small children shriek with joy. The troupe leader says you are the best mountain they have ever had, and pays you a honeycake in wages.

onFailure.narration: You stand on a barrel under a red blanket and RUMBLE. You erupt with a sack of pinecones. Three small children shriek with joy. The troupe leader says you are the best mountain they have ever had, and pays you a honeycake in wages.

scene_campfire_play_tell_true.narration: You describe the hum in every gem. The leader changes the play. Now the mountain is quiet and the falling stones sing. "Much spookier," she whispers. The audience leans closer.

choices.label: Walk on down the line

scene_campfire_play_goat_mountain.narration: Pudding climbs the barrel, wears the red blanket, and eats the script. Her single bleat earns the loudest applause of the night. She bows by mistake.

choices.label: Walk on down the line

scene_campfire_play_rewrite.narration: Your kitsune reads the audience and changes the play on the spot. In the new ending, the stones are not treasure at all. They are a puzzle, and everyone in the play sets off to find out what the puzzle is. The crowd likes it better. The troupe leader writes it down, muttering, "Better. Annoyingly better."

choices.label: Walk on down the line

scene_witch_stall.narration: At a remedy stall, bell charms ring whenever a gem wagon passes. The witch, Mother Thrum, winces over her glasses. "What do you actually want?" she asks. Her pointed hat has a headache remedy tucked in its brim.

choices.label: Ask her a real question: why are the charms ringing?
Ask for something for sore feet

scene_witch_stall_sore_feet.narration: Mother Thrum hands over a sunbloom potion. "Feet next. Listen first." Another wagon makes every charm ring. She closes her eyes and counts to three.

choices.label: Ask a better question

scene_tuned_charm.narration: Mother Thrum gives you a tuned bell charm. Near any gem, it sings the same ancient note. "Older than the road," she says. On her shelf, a stone rings inside a wool sock. Answer her question, or leave that stone with her.

choices.label: Answer her question, truly
Tell her where it fell from, and promise to take it home
Leave the stone in its sock

scene_tuned_charm_leave_it.narration: You leave the ringing stone in its sock. Mother Thrum tucks it behind the counter. "Some questions take longer." You keep the tuned charm and head back to camp.

choices.label: Walk back to your fire

scene_tuned_charm_take_it_home.narration: You tell her where it fell from, and that you mean to take it back. Mother Thrum unwraps the sock. The ringing stops the moment the stone touches your dragonling's hands, as if it has recognized the smell of home. "There," she says softly. "It knows." She gives you the sock as well. "Keep it warm."

choices.label: Walk back to your fire

check_answer.prompt: Tell Mother Thrum what you actually want, and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Mother Thrum listens all the way to the end, then hands you the sock with the stone in it. "That's the Ford Stone. Take it somewhere it stops ringing," she says. "I'd like some sleep."

onFailure.narration: You say something about gems and glory, and Mother Thrum's charms all go quiet at once, which feels like an answer. "Not yet," she says kindly. "Ask yourself again at the mountain."

scene_charm_walk.narration: Your tuned charm sings at passing wagons. Nearby, the wolves lie well away from the gems. Compare the wagon notes, test the wolves' reaction, or compare the sock-wrapped stone if you took it.

choices.label: Hold it to the gem wagons, one after another
Hold it out toward the cinder wolves
Hold it right up against the Ford Stone

check_listen_charm.prompt: Hold the charm to wagon after wagon and listen for a different note

onSuccess.narration: Wagon after wagon, gem after gem, and the note never changes. Not higher. Not lower. Big gems and tiny chips all sing the very same note, as if they all came from one place. One very, very old place.

onFailure.narration: So many wagons, so much singing, that the notes blur together in your head like a choir with a cold. You will have to listen again somewhere quieter. Still, you are sure of one thing: every gem is singing.

scene_charm_walk_wolves.narration: You hold the charm out into the dark where the wolves are lying. It sings. Every wolf flattens its ears, gets up, and moves ten steps farther off, politely, like guests leaving a party early. They are not afraid of you. They are keeping away from the note.

choices.label: Settle in for the night

scene_charm_walk_ford_stone.narration: You hold the charm against the wool sock. The charm and the stone ring together, exactly together, so loudly that every bell in the line answers. Sleepy people sit up and say "WHAT?" Then both go quiet at the very same moment, as if they had finished saying something to each other.

choices.label: Settle in for the night

rest_witch_fire.narration: Rest in the line. The charm chimes at passing wagons, and Pudding visits every supper pot. At dawn, Burdock takes her home. A drover calls numbers from much closer to the water. Your turn is nearly here.

choices.label: Go down to the water at dawn

scene_crossing_verse.narration: At dawn the lead drover sings the crossing verse: slow, slow, wait, slow. "My ford, my pace," he booms. The river is higher. Learn the verse, study the water, or ask for a lesson if he knows you.

choices.label: Learn the crossing verse, line by line
Watch the water instead of the singer
Let the drover who knows you teach you

check_learn_verse.narration: The lead drover sings the crossing verse again and thumps one step on the ground for each line: slow, and slow, and wait, and slow. "Listen first," he booms. "Then sing it back to me, in order."

interaction.cue: Listen to the verse, then sing it back in order.

onSuccess.narration: You hum along under your breath, then a little louder, and by the third time through you are singing it with him. The drover's eyebrows go up. "Huh," he booms. "You've got it." The verse sits in your chest like a steady drum.

onFailure.narration: You learn a verse beautifully, with feeling. It turns out to be the one about turnips that the drovers sing at supper. The drover is far too pleased to tell you until much later.

scene_crossing_verse_watch.narration: The middle current is slower. At the west edge it pulls toward the marsh. You mark the difference: a slip on that edge means a different road. The river has not asked which road you wanted.

choices.label: Go down to the ford

scene_crossing_verse_drover_teaches.narration: "Mudlarks! Here!" The lead drover teaches you each line until you can echo it. His eyebrows conduct the whole lesson. Now you know the easier crossing verse.

choices.label: Go down to the ford

choice_ford.narration: The river is wide and fast. "One wagon at a time," booms the lead drover. Your job in the line matters now: restored markers or a known verse ease the ford roll; the Brackens offer a cart to balance instead. The wagon crew can help if a load tips. Tamsin's unfair Number 1 sends you into the unready crossing.

choices.label: Cross with the caravans, at the drovers' pace
Sing the crossing verse with every step
The drovers you helped wave you in beside the lead wagon
Follow the marker line you put back up
Ride with the Brackens and level their cart load
Use Tamsin's front-of-the-line pebble

check_ford.prompt: Keep your footing in the ford

onSuccess.narration: Step, wait, step. The water pushes and pulls and you do not let it. The lead drover sings the last line of the verse just as your boots hit the north bank.

onFailure.narration: Halfway across, somebody behind you shouts, and then everybody behind you shouts, and the water that was pushing at your knees is suddenly pushing at your waist.

check_ford_easy.prompt: Link arms and wade across together, nice and steady

onSuccess.narration: With friends on every side, the ford is just very wet walking. Somebody up on a wagon starts clapping as you reach the north bank.

onFailure.narration: You are nearly across, with friends on every side, when a yell goes up behind you and the whole river seems to lurch at once.

scene_surge.narration: Halfway across, the red-scarf line-cutters charge into the water behind you, and a wagon full of bread tips over with a SPLASH. Two river drakes surface at once, very interested in the bread. The current is shoving at your knees.

variants.text: Tamsin's shiny pebble is still in your pocket, still saying Number 1. Nobody down here is checking numbers anymore. The river certainly isn't.

choices.label: Toss the drakes their toll: the floating bread
Hold the wagon up, whatever the drakes think
Shout at the red scarves to grab the wagon
Let go and ride the current
Call the wagon crew you freed to brace the tipped load

check_drake_toll.prompt: Fish the floating loaves out of the river and toss each drake its share

onSuccess.narration: The drakes take the bread like a toll collector takes coins, and one of them even nudges the wagon back onto its wheels with its nose. Drovers haul you up the north bank by your collars.

onFailure.narration: One drake takes the bread. The other one wanted the bread you were holding, and it bumps you, very gently, into the deep part.

encounter_drakes.narration: The drakes do not see why a wagon full of bread should stay upright when it could be lunch.

onVictory.narration: The drakes sulk off downstream with one loaf each, and the drovers cheer as you shove the wagon up onto the north bank.

onDefeat.narration: A drake flicks its tail, the wagon goes over, and you go with it, bread and bags and all, off into the current.

scene_surge_scarves_help.narration: "HEY, RED SCARVES!" you shout. The red scarves stare. Then their leader shrugs. "Fair's fair," she says, and the whole gang wades in and grabs the wagon. Together you heave it upright while the drakes squabble over the bread. Everybody staggers up the north bank, soaked to the ears, and the red scarves even say sorry.

choices.label: Climb out on the north bank

end_forded.narration: You stand dripping on the north bank of the west branch, with the whole rush pouring past you toward the mountain. The tuned charm in your pocket is still chiming at every wagon. Behind you, the crossing verse starts again for the next wagon in line. Tonight you camp on the north side, warm and loud and very much in the thick of it.

variants.text: The drover helped with the spilled chips. You remember the catch-and-pass line, and his part in it.
The runner helped check your restored marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work at the tipped load.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across. You did not make that crossing alone.

end_marsh_west.narration: The west branch does what rivers do: it whooshes you west into the green tangles of the Whispering Marsh, past a boggart in a reed hat who applauds. At last the channels let you go on a muddy bank near MossHome, the bigfoot town, at the flooded edge of the Enchanted Woods. You never planned this road, but here you are, and the tuned charm is still humming. The road people will hear about it. The road people hear about everything.

variants.text: The drover helped with the spilled chips. You remember the catch-and-pass line, and his part in it.
The runner helped check your restored marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work at the tipped load.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across. You did not make that crossing alone.

end_swept_setback.narration: The current takes you a long, long way west, through the marsh's tangles and out the far side, three days later than you meant to arrive anywhere. You wash up on the flooded paths of the Enchanted Woods with wet bags, a cold supper, and a drake-shaped grudge. It is not the road you chose, and it cost you time, but you made it out and the charm is still humming.

variants.text: The drover helped with the spilled chips. You remember the catch-and-pass line, and his part in it.
The runner helped check your restored marker line.
The wagon crew repaid your line work at the tipped load.
The Brackens helped balance your ride across. You did not make that crossing alone.

scene_reed_crabs.narration: Two young glassback crabs have parked on the first crossing stones. Wheels approach; claws click; wheels retreat. The lead drover cannot start his verse. "Back to the reeds, please," he booms. The crabs pretend not to hear.

choices.label: Nudge the crabs back to the reeds

encounter_crabs.narration: The crabs clack and shuffle sideways, in no hurry at all. Nudge them off the stones before the whole line loses patience.

scene_crabs_cleared.narration: The crabs shuffle back to the reeds like small dukes leaving a party. The drover gives you a river charm. "Polite neighbors," he booms, and begins his verse.

choices.label: Listen to the verse

scene_crabs_coaxed.narration: The crabs will not move until the drover tips bread crusts down the bank. Off they scuttle. He wraps you in blankets and serves tea. No river charm, but the first step is clear.

choices.label: Listen to the verse

interaction_soup_bowls.narration: The soup tent is just ahead, but empty bowls are rolling out of a basket into the mud. Catch each bowl at the basket rim and stack it safely before the next hungry traveler arrives.

interaction.cue: Tap when a bowl reaches the basket rim.

interaction_clear_lane.narration: Hoofbeats come racing down the line. A relay-runner needs a clear lane, and a loose awning has sagged across the road. Hold its pole up while the people underneath duck out of the way.

interaction.cue: Friends brace the pole while someone lifts the awning.

interaction_evening_echo.narration: As camp settles, travelers tap a welcome on their bowls: tap, tap, rest, tap. You listen, or join in aloud. Around the last fire, the road finally stops asking everyone to hurry.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_dawn_warmup.narration: Morning is cold enough to make every boot creak. Before anyone heads down to the ford, the waiting travelers turn warming up into a game. Stamp, stretch and shake the sleep out of your fingers.

choices.label: Stamp your boots
Reach for the sky
Shake out your fingers

interaction_chip_line.narration: You catch the pannier while the drover gathers his scattered chips. The crowd makes room for your hands. He counts the last handful himself before anyone moves on, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

choices.label: Continue together

interaction_wagon_level.narration: The stuck wagon leans hard into its rut. Raise or lower your side of the load until the marker is in the middle, then roll the wagon out. The drover has named the rut. "Do not encourage it," he says.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side until the wagon load is level.

onSuccess.narration: Level at last. The wagon rolls out with one enormous squelch. The drover gives you a brave whistle and offers his crew's help if a wagon tips in the ford.

onFailure.narration: The wagon comes out in the end, but only after everyone has sat down in the mud at least once. You will be finding mud in your ears until next week.

onAssisted.narration: The drover props the leaning wheel while you level the load. The wagon rolls free. He gives you a brave whistle and promises his crew's help in the ford.

interaction_ford_posts.narration: The marker arrows still face the safe ford approach. Their posts have fallen flat. Brace the ropes while a friend raises them; alone, use the support prop. One arrow points into a cabbage stall. The runner moves that one herself.

interaction.cue: Brace the ropes while the acting hero raises the marker line.

onSuccess.narration: The arrows stand along the checked approach. The runner gives the line one last look before the line moves.

onFailure.narration: The post leans over again. The runner fixes the line while you help clear the lane. You have helped the line, but have not checked the approach yourselves.

onAssisted.narration: The runner takes one rope while you raise the posts. You check the safe approach together.

interaction_bracken_crossing.narration: The Brackens saved a place for you. Their cart rocks as it enters the ford. Keep its load level while the lead drover calls the slow steps. The littlest Bracken holds the bread. This is an important job.

interaction.cue: Raise or lower your side to level the Brackens' cart.
interaction.actionLabel: Bring the cart to the bank

onSuccess.narration: The cart reaches the north bank level. The littlest Bracken lifts the bread in triumph. Helping the family brought you across together.

onFailure.narration: The cart rocks sideways as another wagon tips behind it. The drovers grab the reins while you deal with the surge.

onAssisted.narration: Mother Bracken shifts the sacks while you balance the cart. The drover guides it to the north bank. You crossed with the family's help.

interaction_surge_brace.narration: The crew you freed in the line wades alongside the tipped wagon. They bring the long brace. Hold it in place while the acting hero guides the wheel upright. The drakes argue over the floating bread instead of the instructions.

interaction.cue: Hold the brace while the acting hero rights the wagon.

onSuccess.narration: The brace holds. Your freed wagon crew gets the wheel upright, and everyone reaches the north bank. This is the help you earned in the mud.

onFailure.narration: The wheel turns past the brace. The crew frees you from the tipped load, but the current takes you west.

onAssisted.narration: The lead drover anchors the brace beside the wagon crew. With their help, you right the load and reach the north bank.

choices.label: Continue together
Continue together

interaction_dawn_warmup_response_shake.narration: Somebody wiggles all ten fingers at the river.

choices.label: Continue together

voiceGuide.tone: busy, loud, funny road-camp country; warm underneath, a little spooky at dusk, never scary

npcVoices.burdock: a faun provisioner; cheerful, shameless about his prices, calls everyone 'my lucky number'; owns Pudding, a goat with a weakness for buckets
npcVoices.tamsin: Tamsin Three-Cards, a kitsune card-sharp; quick, delighted to be caught, never sore about losing
npcVoices.wend: a Deep Hollow soup ladler; gentle, generous, asks nothing, says 'kindness first' and means it a little too much
npcVoices.mother_thrum: a ford witch; careful and instructive, peers over glasses, always asks 'what do you actually want?'
npcVoices.drover: the lead drover; slow, booming voice, sings the crossing verse and will not be hurried
npcVoices.relay_runner: a centaur relay-runner; talks while galloping, never finishes a sentence in the same place she started it
npcVoices.brackens: the Brackens, a faun family whose season is over; tired, polite, the littlest one very brave about it
npcVoices.troupe_leader: a rush-camp actor-manager; grand and dramatic, calls everyone 'darlings', thrilled by any eruption
npcVoices.red_scarves: the red-scarf line-cutters' leader; pushy and impatient, but fair when fairly beaten

interaction_chip_line.narration: The chips roll toward the rut. Catch the pannier at your place, then pass it along while the drover gathers the spill. Alone, catch and hand it straight to him. The dog has volunteered to count. Nobody has accepted.

interaction.cue: Catch the pannier, then pass it along the line.

onSuccess.narration: You dive, scoop and pass, scoop and pass, and every chip is back in the pannier before a single pocket gets one. The drover counts them twice, then booms a thank you so loud the horses jump. He will remember your faces.

onFailure.narration: You scoop up a whole double handful, very proudly, and give the drover three chips and a great deal of gravel. He laughs so hard his hat falls off. By the time he finds it, the crowd has pocketed the rest.

onAssisted.narration: The drover anchors the end of your line. Together you catch the spill before it reaches the crowd. He remembers the help, including his own part.

interaction_evening_echo.narration: The camp settles into evening. At the last fire before the remedy stalls, travelers tap a little welcome on their bowls: tap, tap, rest, tap. Listen, then tap it back so the next fire can hear.

interaction.cue: Listen, then repeat the welcome in order.

interaction_dawn_warmup.narration: Morning is cold enough to make every boot creak. Before anyone heads down to the ford, the waiting travelers turn warming up into a game. Stamp, stretch and shake the sleep out of your fingers.

options.label: Shake out your fingers
options.reaction: Somebody wiggles all ten fingers at the river.
